risks: Over 64% of our operating revenue came from our top five customers, though we served between 178-200 customers during the nine months ended December 31, 2024, and the prior three fiscal years.
The loss of any of our top customers, or the loss of revenue from these top customers could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

While we served 189, 184, 178 and 200 customers, respectively during the nine month period ended December 31, 2024 and the Fiscal 2024, Fiscal 2023 and Fiscal 2022, respectively, over 64% of our revenue from operations came from our top five customers during the said period.

Fluctuations in the performance of the industry in which our top five and top ten customers operate may result in a loss of customers, a decrease in the volume of work we undertake or the price at which we offer our products and services.

Our dependence on our top five/ten customers subjects us to various risks which may include, reduction, delay or cancellation of orders, failure to renew contracts, failure to renegotiate favourable terms or the loss of these customers entirely which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations.
There is no assurance that customers will continue to place orders with us at volumes or rates consistent with, and commensurate to, the amount of business received from them historically, or at all.

Our customers typically place orders with us based on their internal requirements, which depend on factors such as, price fluctuations, capacity limitations, demand of end products, dynamic industry trends, etc.
On account of the changing demand of our customers, our top five and top ten customers vary, and we may not receive consist volume of orders from such customers.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: Funding the capital expenditure towards purchase of plant and machinery We are primarily engaged in designing, manufacturing, and supplying a variety of standardised as well as customised battery casings, pail & containers and thinwall containers which are used in various industries such as, vehicle batteries, inverters, paints, agrochemical, lubricants, food and dairy products, etc.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: The details of our Operating Facilities and our products and services have been provided below: Unit Products manufactured Dadra Pails & Thinwall containers Dehradun (Unit-I) Battery casings and Meter boxes Dehradun (Unit-II) Battery casings Hosur (Manufacturing facility) Battery casings and Pails & thinwall containers Panipat Pails & thinwall containers and Meter boxes Una Battery casings and Pails & thinwall containers Hosur (Painting Facility) Painting of automotive components We have a track record of expanding manufacturing capabilities and capacities.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: We had set up our first manufacturing facility in 1999 in Saily (Silvassa) and since then, we have expanded our operations to encompass over seven Operating Facilities.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: On an ongoing basis, we invest in the procurement of plant and machinery, which is utilized by us in carrying out of our business.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: In 2023, we had further diversified our business operations by setting up a Painting Facility in Hosur for painting of automotive parts.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: In the nine month period ended December 31, 2024 and the preceding three Fiscals, we have increased our plant and machinery fixed assets by a total of ₹ 484.60 million.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: We intend to utilise upto ₹ 598.21 million from the Net Proceeds towards capital expenditure to purchase injection moulding machines, injection stretch blow moulding machines, moulds, IML robots and other auxiliary and ancillary machines and equipment.

other_material_facts.label: acquisition_investment
other_material_facts.value: With the investment in machines and robots, we aim to achieve our primary objective of product diversification process addition and increasing production capacity.

other_material_facts.label: capital_expenditure
other_material_facts.value: While we propose to utilize upto ₹ 598.21 million towards purchasing plant and machinery, based on our current estimates, the specific number, nature and location of such proposed plant and machinery to be procured by our Company will be decided in due course, depending on our business requirements, market condition, etc.

other_material_facts.label: debt_repayment
other_material_facts.value: The credit rating of our Company by CareEdge Ratings in the last three fiscals is as under: December 10, 2024 November 17, 2023 November 04, 2022 Long Term Instruments Short Term Instruments Long Term Instruments Short Term Instruments Long Term Instruments Short Term Instruments CARE BBB+; Stable CARE A2 CARE BBB+; Stable CARE A2 CARE BBB+; Positive CARE A3+ Our Company proposes to utilise an estimated amount of up to ₹ 250.00 million out of the Net Proceeds towards repayment/pre-payment, in part or full, of all or a portion of certain existing borrowings availed by our Company.

other_material_facts.label: debt_repayment

other_material_facts.label: acquisition_investment
other_material_facts.value: The repayment/ prepayment, will help reduce our outstanding indebtedness, assist us in achieving a favourable debt-equity ratio, reduce our interest outflow and enable utilisation of some additional amount from our internal accruals for further investment in business growth and expansion, etc.

other_material_facts.label: general_corporate_purposes
other_material_facts.value: General Corporate Purposes We expect to utilize ₹[●] million of the Net Proceeds towards general corporate purposes which shall not exceed 25% of the Gross Proceeds.

other_material_facts.label: general_corporate_purposes
other_material_facts.value: Our Company proposes to deploy the balance Net Proceeds aggregating to ₹ [●] million towards general corporate purposes, subject to such amount not exceeding 25% of the Gross Proceeds, in compliance with the SEBI ICDR Regulations.

other_material_facts.label: general_corporate_purposes
other_material_facts.value: The general corporate purposes for which our Company proposes to utilize Net Proceeds include: i) funding growth opportunities; ii) strengthening marketing capabilities and brand building exercises; iii) meeting ongoing general corporate contingencies; iv) funding capital or operating expenditures; v) funding overheads, salaries & wages and other administrative expenses; vi) executing new projects, buying new assets; vii) meeting finance costs and making payments to Government and other statutory bodies; and viii) any other purpose as may be approved by our Board or a duly appointed committee from time to time, subject to compliance with applicable laws.

other_material_facts.label: acquisition_investment
other_material_facts.value: In accordance the Companies Act, 2013, our Company confirms that, pending utilisation of the proceeds of the Offer as described above, it shall not use the funds from the Net Proceeds for buying, trading or otherwise dealing in shares of any other listed company or for any investment in the equity markets.

other_material_facts.label: general_corporate_purposes
other_material_facts.value: Monitoring Utilization of Funds In terms of Regulation 41 of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, our Company will appoint a monitoring agency to monitor the utilisation of the Gross Proceeds, including the proceeds proposed to be utilised towards general corporate purposes, prior to filing of the Red Herring Prospectus with the RoC.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Over 64% of our operating revenue came from our top five customers, though we served between 178-200 customers during the nine months ended December 31, 2024, and the prior three fiscal years.
- The loss of any of our top customers, or the loss of revenue from these top customers could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
- While we served 189, 184, 178 and 200 customers, respectively during the nine month period ended December 31, 2024 and the Fiscal 2024, Fiscal 2023 and Fiscal 2022, respectively, over 64% of our revenue from operations came from our top five customers during the said period.
- Fluctuations in the performance of the industry in which our top five and top ten customers operate may result in a loss of customers, a decrease in the volume of work we undertake or the price at which we offer our products and services.
- Our dependence on our top five/ten customers subjects us to various risks which may include, reduction, delay or cancellation of orders, failure to renew contracts, failure to renegotiate favourable terms or the loss of these customers entirely which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations.
- There is no assurance that customers will continue to place orders with us at volumes or rates consistent with, and commensurate to, the amount of business received from them historically, or at all.
- Our customers typically place orders with us based on their internal requirements, which depend on factors such as, price fluctuations, capacity limitations, demand of end products, dynamic industry trends, etc.
- On account of the changing demand of our customers, our top five and top ten customers vary, and we may not receive consist volume of orders from such customers.
